_meta.indication: Pristiq, a selective serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI), is indicated for the treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 332 (US, 8-week fixed-dose MDD trial of DVS SR 50 mg and 100 mg)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, fixed-dose (50 and 100 mg/day) study; conducted in the United States
pivotal_trials.population: Adult outpatients with major depressive disorder (MDD)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Adjusted mean change from baseline on the HAM-D17 total score at the final on-therapy evaluation
pivotal_trials.n: Placebo n=150, DVS SR 50 mg n=150, DVS SR 100 mg n=147
pivotal_trials.result: Reviewer's analysis found Study 332 essentially negative with overall p-value 0.054 (LSM change placebo -9.57, DVS SR 50 mg -11.49, 100 mg -10.96); the overall p-value was very close to 0.05

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 333 (Europe/South Africa, 8-week fixed-dose MDD trial of DVS SR 50 mg and 100 mg)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, fixed-dose (50 and 100 mg/day) study; conducted in Europe and South Africa
pivotal_trials.population: Adult outpatients with major depressive disorder (MDD)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Adjusted mean change from baseline on the HAM-D17 total score at the final on-therapy evaluation
pivotal_trials.n: Placebo n=161, DVS SR 50 mg n=164, DVS SR 100 mg n=158
pivotal_trials.result: Study 333 was positive: both 50 mg and 100 mg showed statistically significant results versus placebo; LSM change placebo -10.78, DVS SR 50 mg -13.16, 100 mg -13.65; per-dose p-values 0.004 and <0.001 (overall p=0.001)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5% and at least twice placebo in 50/100 mg groups): nausea, dizziness, insomnia, hyperhidrosis, constipation, somnolence, decreased appetite, anxiety, and specific male sexual function disorders. Nausea 22% (50 mg) vs 10% placebo. 12% of 1,834 PriStiq patients discontinued due to an adverse experience vs 3% of 636 placebo patients.
target_moa: Desvenlafaxine succinate is a potent and selective serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI); clinical efficacy is thought to be related to potentiation of these neurotransmitters in the CNS

boxed_warning.content: Suicidality and Antidepressant Drugs: antidepressants increased the risk of suicidal thinking and behavior in children, adolescents, and young adults in short-term studies of MDD and other psychiatric disorders; PriStiq is not approved for use in pediatric patients.

advisory_committee.vote: NDA 21-992 was not referred to an advisory committee for review

description.text: Added indication in adults for maintenance treatment of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD)

citations.quote: - **S-033**, dated April 16, 2012, received April 17, 2012, a “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application that proposes to add data in support of a new indication in adults for desvenlafaxine SR for the maintenance treatment of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) and

description.text: Added pediatric safety/efficacy data for Major Depressive Disorder in patients ages 7 to 17, fulfilling PREA postmarketing requirement

citations.quote: 1229-1 You have agreed to conduct studies to assess the safety and effectiveness of desvenlafaxine succinate as a treatment for Major Depressive Disorder in pediatric patients ages 7 to 17 (children and adolescents). Both children (ages 7 to 11 years) and adolescents (ages 12 to 17) will be equally represented in the samples, and there will be reasonable distribution of both sexes in these age strata.

summary.text: Standard NDA (505(b)) for the treatment of major depressive disorder; FDA first issued an approvable letter on January 22, 2007, and approved the application after the sponsor's complete response. The application was not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: This new drug application provides for the use of Pristiq (desvenlafaxine succinate) tablets for the treatment of major depressive disorder.
The August 29, 2007 submission constituted a complete response to our January 22, 2007 action letter.

NDA 21-992 was not referred to an advisory committee for review because there are several previously approved agents in the antidepressant class of drugs, evaluation of the safety data did not reveal particular safety issues that were unexpected for this class, and the design and results of the efficacy trials did not pose particular concerns.

requirement.text: Deferred pediatric studies under PREA: assess safety and effectiveness of desvenlafaxine succinate for MDD in pediatric patients ages 7 to 17; final report 4.5 years from approval

citations.quote: You have agreed to conduct studies to assess the safety and effectiveness of desvenlafaxine succinate as a treatment for Major Depressive Disorder in pediatric patients ages 7 to 17 (children and adolescents).
**Final Report Submission:** 4.5 years from the date of approval

requirement.text: Exploration of dose response for effectiveness: randomized controlled study including placebo and DVS doses of 10, 25, and 50 mg/day, with a validated and reliable outcome measure to assess for sexual dysfunction; results no later than 3 years after approval

citations.quote: You have agreed to conduct and submit the results of a randomized controlled study including placebo and DVS doses of 10, 25, and 50 mg/day as a Postmarketing commitment. This study will assess efficacy in this dose range and will also include a validated and reliable outcome measure to assess for sexual dysfunction. You have agreed to submit the results of this trial no later than 3 years after the date of the approval for this NDA.

requirement.text: Long-term efficacy study: randomized withdrawal study to address longer-term efficacy at appropriate doses; results no later than approximately 5.5 years from approval

citations.quote: Once you have established the lower end of the dose-response curve for efficacy, you have agreed to conduct and submit the results of a randomized withdrawal study to address longer-term efficacy for your drug at appropriate doses.
**Final Report Submission:** 5.5 years from the date of approval

requirement.text: Sexual dysfunction: acute randomized controlled trial with placebo, 50, and 100 mg/day employing a validated and reliable outcome measure to assess sexual dysfunction; results approximately 5.5 years from approval

citations.quote: agreed to conduct another acute, randomized controlled trial with placebo, 50, and 100 mg/day, and employ a validated and reliable outcome measure to assess for sexual dysfunction. This study could be conducted in parallel with the longer-term efficacy trial, and the results could be submitted approximately 5.5 years from the date of approval for this NDA.

requirement.text: Pharmacology/Toxicology: conduct a standard embryo-fetal toxicity study in rats; results no later than 3 years after approval

citations.quote: Consequently, you have agreed to conduct a standard embryo-fetal toxicity study in rats, and submit the results no later than 3 years after the date of the approval for this NDA.
The August 29, 2007 submission constituted a complete response to our January 22, 2007 action letter.

basis.text: Approvable letter cited CMC issues, need for agreement on dissolution method/specification, a risk management plan for possible overdose toxicity, postmarketing commitments (longer-term efficacy, pediatric, dose response, repeat embryo-fetal toxicity study), and draft labeling

citations.quote:
- Several CMC issues needed to be addressed
- Needed agreement on dissolution method and specification
- Risk management plan: the letter posed a number of questions and made a number of requests regarding a risk management plan for possible overdose toxicity (related to concerns raised about the parent compound, venlafaxine)
